section_title: Incentive Structures and the Political Economy of Research Data
primary_evidence_rule: package verbatim source sentences authoritative; abstracts spot-checked where noted; no blocking on network

findings.location: Paragraph 5 (structural pessimism / crisis discourse); relevant to whole section framing
findings.claim_text: The section presents the reproducibility/irreproducibility crisis as unambiguously genuine throughout (e.g., 'the multi-site replication projects and standing laboratory networks that first exposed the crisis'), and cites Ioannidis2005b for 'most published research findings are false'. The contrarian position that the crisis NARRATIVE itself is empirically mistaken is entirely absent.
findings.issue: Suppressed conflict (package conflict #8, resolution_status: open, and explicitly flagged in the task brief). Ioannidis2005b (paper A: most findings likely false) is cited (conflict box at lines 46-49), but Fanelli2018 (paper B: 'this narrative is mistaken... a narrative of epochal changes and empowerment of scientists would be more accurate') is not cited anywhere (grep count 0). The section presents a clean 'crisis is real' consensus when the package holds an open conflict on whether the crisis narrative is genuine. Per calibration, conflict suppression is the most important failure mode.
findings.evidence: Package finding Fanelli2018 (10.1073/pnas.1708272114): 'This article provides an overview of recent evidence suggesting that this narrative is mistaken...'. Conflict #8 nature_of_conflict: 'Whether science faces a genuine reproducibility/false-findings crisis... bears directly on how urgently incentive/reform interventions are justified.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence acknowledging the contrarian view, e.g. in paragraph 5 or the structural-pessimism conflict box: 'A minority position holds that the crisis narrative is itself overstated and that a story of methodological empowerment would be more accurate {cite:p}`Fanelli2018`, though the stagnation-of-power evidence weighs against reading the problem as resolved.' Cite both sides.

findings.location: Paragraph 9 (line 44): '...modelling shows how, when negative results publish at a small fraction of the rate of positive ones, false claims can be canonised as fact {cite:p}`Nissen2016`.'
findings.claim_text: Nissen2016 (publication bias canonises false facts) is cited as settled, but the contrarian model that publishing potentially non-replicable / positive-only studies can maximise the community's efficiency of knowledge gain is omitted.
findings.issue: Suppressed conflict (package conflict #4, resolution_status: open). Nissen2016 is cited; Lewandowsky2020 (grep count 0) is absent. The section presents the publication-bias-corrupts-the-record view as uncontested when the package flags an open disagreement about whether publishing non-replicable studies is inefficient (Nissen) or efficient (Lewandowsky & Oberauer).
findings.evidence: Package finding Lewandowsky2020 (10.1038/s41467-019-14203-0): 'We find that the publication of potentially non-replicable studies minimizes cost and maximizes efficiency of knowledge gain for the scientific community under a variety of assumptions.' Conflict #4 pits this against Nissen2016's canonization model.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the counter-model near the Nissen2016 citation, e.g.: 'though a competing model argues that publishing potentially non-replicable studies and replicating selectively can be efficient for the community {cite:p}`Lewandowsky2020`.' This restores the open conflict.

findings.location: Paragraph on incentives-already-shifting (line 65): '...a citation advantage documented for open access and open data across large scientometric samples {cite:p}`Klebel2025, Migliorini2026, Friederichs2026`...'
findings.claim_text: The section groups Klebel2025 with Migliorini2026 and Friederichs2026 as jointly 'documenting' an open-access/open-data citation advantage across large samples, presenting the advantage as an established, convergent fact.
findings.issue: Conflict presented as resolved (package conflict #12, resolution_status: open). Both keys are present (mechanical pre-check passes), but the substance of the conflict is erased: Klebel2025 is a scoping review that found the open-access citation advantage INCONSISTENT (only 47.8% of studies found it; 27.6% found none; 23.9% only in subsets), whereas Friederichs2026 reports a clear ~23% single-field advantage. Citing Klebel2025 as 'documenting a citation advantage' is an interpretive mismatch that suppresses its skeptical conclusion about open access. (Klebel2025 does support the narrower open-DATA sub-claim at ~9% more citations, so the mismatch is partial, not total.)
findings.evidence: Package finding Klebel2025 (10.1098/rsos.241248): '47.8% of reviewed studies found an OACA, with the remaining studies finding no OACA (27.6%) or only in subsets (23.9%).' Conflict #12: 'Whether open access confers a citation advantage: the scoping review finds it inconsistent... whereas the single-field empirical study reports a clear ~23% advantage.'
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the sentence, e.g.: 'a citation advantage that is real but inconsistent across studies for open access {cite:p}`Klebel2025` while clearer in single-field analyses {cite:p}`Friederichs2026, Migliorini2026`, and reasonably robust (~9% more citations) for open data {cite:p}`Klebel2025`.' Do not present Klebel2025 as unqualified evidence for the advantage.

findings.location: Paragraph on declared-vs-actual (line 19): '...in a live individual-participant-data meta-analysis, only a minority of contacted trialists responded and only a fifth of responders shared their data {cite:p}`Flanagan2026`.'
findings.claim_text: 'only a minority of contacted trialists responded'
findings.issue: Quantitative attribution error (direction inverted). Flanagan2026 found that a MAJORITY of contacted trialists responded (48 of 79 = 60.8%), not a minority. The second clause ('only a fifth of responders shared', 20.8%) is correct. The section understates the response rate, inverting majority to minority.
findings.evidence: Package finding Flanagan2026 (10.11124/jbies-24-00548): 'Trialists from 48 of 79 trials (60.8%) responded to the IPD-MA invitation' and 'Of the trialists who responded, 10 (20.8%) shared IPD and 38 (79.2%) did not.'
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite to preserve the true numbers, e.g.: 'even after contacting trialists directly, most responded but only a fifth of responders — roughly one in eight of all those approached — shared their data {cite:p}`Flanagan2026`.'

findings.location: Coverage of evidence package (uncited paper) — relevant to paragraph on preregistration being hollowed (line 67): '...badges and mandates strip preregistration of its methodological function rather than delivering it {cite:p}`Vize2024, Bertin2025`.'
findings.claim_text: The section's claim that preregistration can be 'gamed or hollowed out' and 'no less likely to report positive results' is supported by commentary (Vize2024, Bertin2025) and one matched comparison (vandenAkker2023), but the direct empirical demonstration that even structured preregistration leaves residual analytic flexibility is not cited.
findings.issue: SHOULD_CITE. Bakker2020 provides direct empirical evidence — comparing 105 preregistrations, structured formats restricted researcher degrees of freedom better than unstructured (large effect) but neither eliminated them, and coders agreed on the number of hypotheses only 14% of the time. This materially strengthens the section's claim that preregistration is imperfect / hollowable, which is currently carried by opinion pieces.
findings.evidence: Package finding Bakker2020 (10.1371/journal.pbio.3000937): 'Coders agreed on the number of hypotheses in only 14.29% of the scores'; 'The difference was large (Cliff's Delta = 0.49).' It operationalises the Wicherts2016 degrees-of-freedom taxonomy already cited.
findings.suggested_fix: Add Bakker2020 to the preregistration-limits discussion, e.g.: 'empirically, even structured preregistration reduces but does not eliminate researcher degrees of freedom, and independent coders often cannot agree on how many hypotheses a preregistration even states {cite:p}`Bakker2020`.' Writer may instead document a waiver arguing vandenAkker2023 + Wicherts2016 already cover 'preregistration is imperfect'.

findings.location: Fraud paragraph (line 58): 'Image-duplication screening of more than twenty thousand articles set an early baseline of several percent containing inappropriately duplicated images, and {cite:t}`Richardson2025` show the broker entities...'
findings.claim_text: The >20,000-article / 'several percent' image-duplication baseline is attributed to Richardson2025.
findings.issue: Trace-to-primary-data: the 3.8% image-duplication figure is not Richardson2025's own measurement — Richardson2025 repeats it from a prior systematic analysis (Bik et al., its reference 24). The package curated the claim to Richardson2025, and the section's 'set an early baseline' framing is honest, but the number is a secondary citation, not primary data from the cited paper.
findings.evidence: Package finding Richardson2025 (10.1073/pnas.2420092122) source sentence: 'A systematic analysis of more than 20,000 articles... reported that 3.8% of these articles contained inappropriately duplicated images... (24).' The '(24)' marks it as a citation to another study.
findings.suggested_fix: Either attribute the baseline to the primary source or signal the secondary nature, e.g.: 'an early systematic screen of more than twenty thousand articles reported several percent with inappropriately duplicated images (baseline cited in {cite:t}`Richardson2025`), which now shows the broker entities enabling fraud are large and growing.'

findings.location: Animal-welfare-stake paragraph (line 27): '...a cardiovascular-literature audit finding fewer than two percent of papers fully reproducible confirms that the problem is systemic rather than confined to one specialty {cite:p}`Heckerman2025`.'
findings.claim_text: 'confirms that the problem is systemic rather than confined to one specialty'
findings.issue: Mild scope inflation. A single cardiovascular audit (639 articles, 3 journals) plus one animal-opioid audit (Blackwell2025) is used to assert the problem is 'systemic rather than confined to one specialty'. Two specialties does not by itself establish systematicity; the load-bearing 'systemic' claim leans on the broader section evidence base rather than these two audits.
findings.evidence: Package finding Heckerman2025 (10.7554/elife.81051): '<2% fully reproducible' in Circulation/EHJ/JACC — a single specialty. 'systemic rather than confined to one specialty' is an inference beyond one audit.
findings.suggested_fix: Soften to 'adds a second specialty to the same pattern' or explicitly ground the systemic claim in the multi-field evidence already marshalled (psychology, clinical, ecology), e.g.: 'echoes the same pattern seen across psychology and clinical medicine, indicating it is not confined to one specialty.'

findings.location: Paragraph 4 (line 15): 'The pattern generalises across national systems — in Ecuador, reliance on journal-centric metrics predicted lower adoption of open practices...{cite:p}`Guerra2026`.'
findings.issue: A single-country (Ecuador) mixed-methods study is used to headline a claim that the pattern 'generalises across national systems'. The generalisation is defensible against the earlier international (Rice2020) and US/Canada (McKiernan2019) evidence, but Guerra2026 alone is one national system.
findings.evidence: Package finding Guerra2026 (10.3389/frma.2025.1707881): single Ecuador study, OR 0.72 (journal metrics) vs 1.65 (institutional support).
findings.suggested_fix: Phrase as an additional instance rather than proof of generalisation, e.g.: 'and the same pattern appears in national systems as different as Ecuador, where...'.

findings.location: Rebuttal paragraph (line 67): 'coordinated replication efforts in fields beyond psychology continue to report low success rates {cite:p}`Murphy2025a`'
findings.issue: Minor system inflation: 'fields' (plural) is cited to a single field (sports and exercise science). The plural implies broader coverage than one study.
findings.evidence: Package finding Murphy2025a (10.1007/s40279-025-02200-x): sports and exercise science replication project, 28% successful.
findings.suggested_fix: Singularise: 'coordinated replication in fields beyond psychology, such as sports and exercise science, continues to report low success rates {cite:p}`Murphy2025a`.'

findings.location: QRP prevalence paragraph (line 31) and figure fig-sec7-qrp-prevalence (line 36)
findings.claim_text: Fanelli2009 (~2% FFP, up to a third other QRPs), Schneider2024 (94% used at least one QRP, frequency far lower), Velicu2025 (~one fifth implicitly associate QRPs with success).
findings.issue: POSITIVE NOTE / no fix needed. The section and its figure caption correctly keep the three constructs separate (self-admitted serious FFP vs any-QRP self-admission vs implicit attitudinal association), explicitly flag the 2-to-94 spread as a severity/breadth artifact, and mark Fanelli's own ~34% any-QRP as the like-for-like comparator to Schneider's 94%. This directly satisfies the task's Track 1/2 caution against conflating different-construct prevalences.
findings.evidence: Figure caption (line 36) reproduces the package's mandatory_caption_caveats verbatim; conflict box (lines 39-42) presents John2012 vs Schneider2024 as method-resolved.
findings.suggested_fix: None required — retained as evidence the conflation risk was handled well.

suppressed_conflicts.topic: Whether the reproducibility/false-findings crisis is genuine (most-findings-false framework vs 'crisis narrative is mistaken'). Paper B entirely absent from section. FLAGGED in task brief.
Whether publishing potentially non-replicable / positive-only studies corrupts the record (canonization) or maximises community efficiency. Paper B entirely absent from section.

Whether open access confers a citation advantage (scoping review finds it inconsistent, <half of studies) vs single-field ~23% advantage. Both keys present, but section presents the advantage as convergent/resolved, suppressing Klebel2025's skeptical conclusion.
suppressed_conflicts.note: Represented mechanically (both keys present) but the conflict is presented as resolved — counted as suppressed on substance.

narrative: Section 07 is broadly well-evidenced, quantitatively careful, and unusually good at exactly the trap the brief warned about: its QRP paragraph and figure caption rigorously separate self-admitted serious FFP (~2%, Fanelli2009), any-QRP admission (94%, Schneider2024), and implicit attitudinal association (~20%, Velicu2025), explicitly naming the 2-to-94 spread a severity/breadth artifact and flagging Fanelli's own ~34% as the like-for-like comparator. The Freedman2015 US$28B figure is model-caveated as an order-of-magnitude claim. Nine of twelve package conflicts are genuinely represented as live tensions (five in dedicated conflict boxes). No hallucinated citations: all 133 cite_keys resolve to the citemap (Ioannidis2005b is citemap-only, not a package finding, and is used validly). The coverage accounting invariant holds exactly: 132 cited + 3 should_cite + 10 out-of-scope + 30 redundant + 0 low-quality = 175 papers in package, with 43 uncited papers each classified once. The failures are concentrated in conflict survival: two open conflicts are entirely one-sided — Fanelli2018 ('the crisis narrative is mistaken', the brief-flagged conflict) and Lewandowsky2020 ('publishing non-replicable studies is efficient') are absent while their partners (Ioannidis2005b, Nissen2016) are cited — and a third (the open-access citation advantage, Klebel2025 vs Friederichs2026) is presented as convergent when Klebel2025 actually found it inconsistent across <half of studies. One quantitative error inverts Flanagan2026's majority (60.8%) response rate to a 'minority'. Bakker2020 is a should-cite that would empirically ground the preregistration-hollowing claim. Five MUST_FIX, two SHOULD_CAVEAT, three MINOR; conflict survival 0.75 (above the 0.5 blanket-return threshold, so the fixes are targeted rather than a full re-roll).
